# Angular Routing Specialist Skill

**Category:** Tech Skills > Frontend > Angular

## Purpose

Provides specialized knowledge, step-by-step procedures, and quality standards for Angular Routing Specialist operations using Angular technology. This skill encapsulates technology-specific best practices, design patterns, performance optimization techniques, and production-grade implementation guidance for Angular within Frontend development.

## When to Use

- When configuring Angular routing with lazy-loaded modules
- When implementing route guards for authentication and authorization
- When setting up nested routing with child routes
- When Angular-specific technical expertise is required
- When best practices for Angular technology stack must be applied
- When production-grade Angular implementation guidance is needed

## Capabilities

- Configure lazy-loaded feature modules with loadChildren
- Implement CanActivate, CanDeactivate, and Resolve guards
- Design nested routing hierarchies with named outlets
- Set up preloading strategies for optimal performance
- Handle route parameters and query parameters effectively

## Procedure

1. Analyze application navigation requirements
2. Design route hierarchy with lazy loading boundaries
3. Implement route guards and resolvers
4. Configure preloading strategy
5. Set up route animations and transitions
6. Test routing with RouterTestingModule

## Anti-Hallucination Rules

- Do not mix standalone and module-based routing without version check
- Verify guard interface changes between Angular versions
- Do not fabricate version numbers, API endpoints, or library names
- Always cite the specific documentation, RFC, or standard being referenced
- If technology-specific data is unavailable, explicitly state the gap and request clarification
- Never assume features exist in a specific version without verification

## Quality Checks

- All routes have proper guards where needed
- Lazy loading boundaries minimize initial bundle
- Route resolvers handle error states
- All code examples must be syntactically valid and tested
- Cross-reference findings against official documentation
- Flag any assumptions made during analysis with explicit markers
- Validate all performance claims with reproducible benchmarks
- Ensure all recommendations follow Angular community best practices
